title: workbench-command.v1
description: Everything a browser is permitted to submit, and nothing else. A publication id, a published subject, editable values keyed by declared pointer, an optional example selection, and a request identity for deduplication. `additionalProperties: false` is the enforcement, not the documentation: a canonical envelope, namespace override, fixed-field override, provider inventory or endpoint selection has no place to go in this shape.

requestId.description: Client-generated request identity. The service persists the request-to-run association before initiating any external effect, so a repeat of the same requestId reconciles to the same run rather than executing twice. Disabling a button is not duplicate-execution protection.

publicationId.description: Which publication this command was composed against. A mismatch is a stale publication and is refused.

subject.description: A published capability subject. The server resolves it to a namespace and plan; the browser never names either.

editableValues.description: Values keyed by JSON pointer. Every key must be declared editable for this subject by the publication's ownership declaration. An undeclared or non-editable pointer is refused rather than ignored.

exampleSelection.description: Which retained example to run, for subjects whose input the server owns entirely. Must be in the publication's allow-list for this subject. The example's payload is never carried here.

expectedDraftRevision.description: Optional optimistic revision check. Changing input invalidates a previously displayed result.
